subject: Hosted API — short privacy/terms snippets for Console & Sales
messages:
From: Anna Schultz <anna@fintegrity.com>
To: mina_haddad@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@fintegrity.com
Date: Tue, 15 Sep 2026 08:12:00 -0400
Subject: Quick ask — short DPA / console language for Hosted API

Hi Mina,

Thanks again for the demo last week — product looked great. Our legal & procurement teams asked for two short items we can include in our vendor assessment deck: (1) a one-sentence customer-facing explanation of how Redwood's Hosted API handles cross-border transfers (high level, plain language) and (2) a 1–2 line blurb describing subprocessors and how customers can request the subprocessor list. They want something short and non-legal for our engineers and privacy team to read quickly.

We attached a short questionnaire with context. Can you share a draft snippet we can put into our vendor summary by EOD Thursday? Also flag if any of this is an SLA/contractual ask that needs legal review.

Appreciate it — Anna

--
Anna Schultz
Head of Security & Compliance
Fintegrity Analytics
anna@fintegrity.com

From: mina_haddad@redwood.com
To: Anna Schultz <anna@fintegrity.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, kimberly_park@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 15 Sep 2026 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick ask — short DPA / console language for Hosted API

Anna — thanks, glad the demo was useful. Looping in Laura (sales) and Kimberly (privacy/product) to draft.

Quick notes for expectation-setting: the public-facing snippets can be purely explanatory (non-contractual). Anything that references commitments (data retention windows, processors used for specific regions) should call out that customers can see the detailed DPA/subprocessor list after engagement or via our Console for enterprise customers.

We'll produce: 1) a one-sentence cross-border transfers blurb, 2) a 1–2 line subprocessor explanation, and 3) an optional short pointer to where customers can request the full list or view it in the Console / procurement channel.

Will aim to return a first pass within 24 hours.

Best,
Mina

--
Mina Haddad
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
mina@redwood.com

From: kimberly_park@redwood.com
To: mina_haddad@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 16 Sep 2026 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Proposed public snippets (for review)

Folks — first pass below. Kept language non-legal and product-friendly, called out where to escalate to Legal if a customer treats this as contractual.

1) Cross-border transfers (one sentence):
"Redwood routes inference requests to the nearest available regional capacity; when data moves across borders to provide the service, we rely on standard contractual safeguards and documented transfer measures — you can request details specific to your account during onboarding."

2) Subprocessors (1–2 lines):
"We work with a limited set of service providers (subprocessors) to operate the Hosted API (e.g., cloud infra, observability). Customers can request the current subprocessor list, and enterprise customers can review the list in the Console or via their procurement contact."

Notes / flags:
- "Standard contractual safeguards" is intentionally broad. If Fintegrity requires specific SCC references or mechanistic descriptions (e.g., encryption in transit + model cache retention windows), we should escalate to Legal.
- We should avoid naming cloud partners in a one-line public blurb — keep that for the subprocessor list.

Attaching a cleaned DPA snippet and the Fintegrity questionnaire answers.

Kimberly

--
Kimberly Park
Privacy & Policy Manager, Redwood Inference
kimberly@redwood.com

From: laura_bennett@redwood.com
To: Anna Schultz <anna@fintegrity.com>
Cc: mina_haddad@redwood.com, kimberly_park@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 17 Sep 2026 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick ask — short DPA / console language for Hosted API

Anna — thanks for the patience. Attaching the short snippets and a one-pager we typically share with procurement. Paste below so you can drop into your deck immediately.

Cross-border transfers (public-facing):
"Redwood operates regional inference capacity; when requests are routed across regions, we protect transfers with standard contractual safeguards and technical controls. For account-specific transfer details, please request the DPA addendum through your procurement contact."

Subprocessors (public-facing):
"We engage a small, vetted set of subprocessors to run and monitor the Hosted API. The up-to-date subprocessor list is available to customers on request; enterprise customers may view it directly in the Console once under contract."

If Fintegrity needs explicit SCC/SCC-equivalent references or certified transfer mechanisms, we can loop in Legal and provide a contractual reference. Otherwise these lines should be fine for the vendor slide.

Best regards,
Laura Bennett
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
laura@redwood.com

Attachments: DPA_snippet_draft_v1.docx; Fintegrity_questions_09-15.pdf
